vikisozluk_etimolojiler.metin: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Form XI (اِفْعَالَّ (ifʕālla)) of the root ش ع ن (š ʕ n), built on the elative or colour-quality pattern, analogous to Form XI اِدْهَامَّ (idhāmma) from أَدْهَم (ʔadham). The root carries a base sense of dishevelment, dispersal, and bristling. Form IX اِشْعَنَّ (išʕanna) denotes the simple inchoative — hair puffing outward — while Form XI اِشْعَانَّ (išʕānna) denotes the intensive or extended state: hair not merely ruffled but fully splayed, separated, and standing on end. The verbal noun اِشْعِينَان (išʕīnān) follows the Form XI pattern اِفْعِيلَال (ifʕīlāl), the geminate lam realised as ن-ن in accordance with the root's third radical, yielding the attested form اِشْعِينَاناً (išʕīnānan) (Lisān, al-Ṣiḥāḥ, Tāj).
